after.en: Zero-upsample first, then run a kernel over it: that is a transposed convolution with stride 2, and the kernel decides which neighbours, in what proportion, fill the empty cells. The decoder of a segmentation network uses it to enlarge small feature maps layer by layer back to the size of the picture.

t.en: The networks of earlier chapters make the picture smaller and smaller: pooling and downsampling shrink 16×16 to a few numbers that answer "what is this?". But to ask "what is every pixel?", the answer has to be as big as the original.
The new primitive <part-ref to="part:zeroUp"></part-ref> doubles the size: each pixel goes in the top left of a 2×2 block, and the other three cells are 0.
Your task in this level: enlarge an 8×8 picture to 16×16, every pixel becoming a 2×2 block of the same value.

brief.en: Enlarge an 8×8 picture to 16×16: every pixel becomes a 2×2 block, all four cells the same.

hint.en: <part-ref to="part:zeroUp"></part-ref> puts each pixel in the top left of its 2×2. Where do the other three cells get their number?
